zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical reference consulted after independent scan reading: NINJAL, *Entry Words Data of Nippojisho*, version 202510, developed by Hideyuki Ohshima with assistance from Taichi Aida ([official release](https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html)), licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). This review’s transcription corrections and explanatory notes are distinct from the supplied dataset.

lines.note: Tsuridooro is a hanging lantern. The circumflex in dôro is visible and retained; the Portuguese specifies suspension rather than a standing lamp.
Tsuri ito is fishing line, directly matched by linha de pescar. The headword has the cedilla of tç, which the OCR omitted.
Tsurimono means a suspended object; the gloss narrows this general meaning to a particular utensil below. The colon and divided particular- are visible.

runs.text: mente ſe toma por hũa panela de ferro, que ſer

lines.note: Completes particularmente and identifies an iron pot. The printed line ends with ser, continuing as ue below, without a supplied terminal hyphen; ferro has the two r types.
Ser-ue is the historical spelling of serve, completing the description of a pot used in chanoyu, the preparation and service of tea. Chanoyu is a Japanese term embedded in the Portuguese explanation.

Tsuuriqi denotes supernatural powers, introduced as penetrating powers or glorious qualities. The sequence tçǔriqi is supported by the types and the bundled NINJAL entry; the OCR's Teǔiriqi was malformed.

The explanation enumerates six powers. Iinqiǒtçǔ is the first, the power of supernatural movement explained below; the faint narrow i between q and ǒ is retained from the enlarged scan, not silently omitted as in the OCR.
The first power is glossed as speed of movement. Tenguentçǔ introduces heavenly sight as the second; the printed n and t before çǔ restore the corrupted OCR ending.
The second power sees through everything. Tenni- begins the third power, heavenly hearing; the two n types are retained rather than OCR Tenmi, and the physical division is preserved.

runs.text: Ouuir todas as couſas do mundo. Quar

lines.note: Tçǔ completes Tenni-tçǔ. Its gloss is hearing everything in the world; Quar continues as ta on the next row, with no added hyphen at the right edge.

Quar-ta introduces the fourth power, knowing everyone's heart or thoughts. The scan appears to print Taxin çǔ without a t before çǔ; this anomalous but usable reading is retained rather than regularized to the expected tsuu spelling.
Rojintçǔ is the fifth power, freedom from stain or imperfection. The o after R is abraded but has no securely visible long-vowel mark, so none is supplied from the expected Buddhist term.

Completes the fifth definition and names the sixth power, knowledge of previous lives or the past. Xucumiǒtçǔ replaces the OCR's extra a and confused t; the final length mark is faint but best read as a caron like the neighboring çǔ forms.
Sa-ber completes the preceding line's verb: knowing all the past. The ß-shaped sort is preserved rather than expanded into a different sequence.
Tsurisage, tsurisaguru, tsurisageta means hanging something down. The headword's u and long ſ are visible; cou continues as ſa below without an invented line-end hyphen.
Completes cousa pera baixo, an object suspended downward. This short continuation belongs to tsurisage and is not a separate entry.
Tsuritoodai is a hanging lamp or lampstand. Candieiro is the printed Portuguese spelling; the circumflex distinguishes the actual tô type from a normalized long-vowel notation.
Tsuriudo is a fisherman using a rod. The gloss reads pescador, with a d rather than the OCR's ci, and the marked u in the Japanese form is retained.
Tsurizao is a fishing rod. The historical zauo spelling is preserved, with the Portuguese confirming the object rather than a person.
Tsuuro is explained by tooru michi, a road one passes along. Paſ- starts the divided Portuguese verb, while the Japanese synonym remains roman and is not a typeface-toggle target.
The gloss completes passa ou anda. Tsuuro ga tomatta begins an example about a blocked route; the alternative marker l introduces qireta on the following row.

runs.text: Estão os caminhos tomados, ou im-

lines.note: Qireta gives the alternative 'cut off'; the translation says the roads are occupied or obstructed. The divided im- belongs to impedidos below, and the source's provisional st allograph is retained.
Completes impedidos, 'obstructed'. This short physical row closes the blocked-road example before the unrelated crane entry.
Tsuru here means the crane bird, glossed grou. It must remain separate from the homonymous bowstring entry immediately below.
Tsuru now means a bowstring. Tsuru wo sasu is glossed as making bowstrings; the damaged initial is the same T form as neighboring entries, not OCR F.
Fa-zer completes 'make bowstrings'. Tsuruoto wo furu introduces sounding or testing the string; the printed votouo sequence is retained rather than modernized to an expected segmentation.

runs.text: Prouar com a mão a corda fazendoa ſoar.

lines.note: The example means testing the string with the hand by making it sound. The tilde belongs to a in mão, and the historical joined fazendoa is retained.
Tsuru wo kakuru means putting the string on the bow. The scan supplies this physical row only once; the overlapping OCR c1-l029 was a duplicate detection, not additional text.
Tsuru wo hazusu is removing the bowstring, directly matched by tirar. The overlapping OCR c1-l031 repeats the beginning of this same row and is removed without loss of text.
Tsurube is a bucket, specifically relevant to the well-bucket expressions that follow. The initial T and the medial u are faint but compatible with the repeated tsurube forms below.
Tsurubedachi and tsurubedachini describe the vertical manner associated with a hanging well bucket. Feição begins the Portuguese explanation of that manner; the first letter is F, not OCR T.

runs.text: de quem poem, ou dependura balde em poço

lines.note: Explains lowering or hanging a bucket in a well. This supplies the physical image for the steep or sheer feature described on the next rows.

runs.text: pera declarar couſa imgreme como rocha talha-

lines.note: The expression denotes something steep, like a cut rock face. Enlargement supports the printed imgreme spelling; it is retained rather than regularized to modern íngreme. Talha- continues as da below.
Completes talhada and adds a great precipice. The definition concerns a sheer drop, not a different kind of bucket.

runs.text: Corda do balde de tirar agoa.

lines.note: Tsurubenawa is the rope of a bucket used to draw water. The scan and surrounding tsurube entries support naua rather than OCR uaua; agoa is left in its historical spelling.
Tsurubukuro is a bag for the bowstring. The scan gives saco da corda, correcting the OCR's Saro and de, without confusing this string compound with the preceding well-bucket terms.

runs.text: Aſelha da corda do arco por on-

lines.note: Tsurukabura denotes the loop or eye of the bowstring. On- begins onde, whose continuation explains how the loop is fitted to the bow.

runs.text: de ſe mete, & poem no arco.

lines.note: Completes onde: the loop is the part through which the string is put onto the bow. The short continuation closes the preceding technical definition.

runs.text: Official de cordas de arco, que tẽ

lines.note: Tsurukake denotes a maker or worker of bowstrings. The following relative clause describes the trade's distinctive clothing; the abbreviated tẽ is retained.

runs.text: particular trajo em Iapão. ſ. touca na cabeça,

lines.note: The worker has a particular costume in Japan, specified as a head covering. The abraded wording is particular trajo; the Portuguese abbreviation ſ. introduces the particulars.
Adds a short red katabira garment to the costume. Catabira is a Japanese clothing term embedded in the Portuguese sentence; the central tabira types survive sufficiently to correct the OCR's Cavira.
This separate tsurukake entry refers the reader to tsurunabe, the iron-pot entry in the next column. Its left alignment is restored; it is not a continuation of the preceding costume description.

runs.text: Hũa laya de bules de vinho d

lines.note: Tsurukubi names a type of crane-necked wine vessel. The headword and laya are heavily abraded but supported by the surviving strokes and the following compound; only d is securely visible at the right edge, so an expected final e is not supplied.

runs.text: bronzo como galhetas grandes, ou guindes.

lines.note: The vessels are bronze, compared with large cruets or guindes. Guindes is retained as the visible historical vessel-name rather than replaced with a more familiar modern term.

Tsurukubi no fiotan denotes crane-necked gourds. The damaged cubi sequence is supported by the preceding headword and bundled NINJAL identification; no secure circumflex is visible over fiotan here, despite the index's marked form.

runs.text: ço como de grou. ¶ Item, Qualquer outro

lines.note: Completes pescoço, a neck like a crane's, and broadens the term to other vessels. The right-edge letters of Qualquer outro are pale; the surviving forms and the following vaſo support the chosen reading.
Completes the extension to any vessel of this shape or form. The abraded initial vaſo is recovered from the visible v, a, and long-ſ remnants in the same physical row, not inserted as a new line.
Tsurugi is a sharply cutting sword. The abbreviated Itẽ introduces a broader gloss below; its abbreviation mark is retained.
Adds 'a sword in general' to the preceding definition. Catana is used as a noun within the Portuguese explanation, rather than being a new Japanese headword.

runs.text: Hum aparelho de rota em que em

lines.note: Tsurumaki is a rattan apparatus for winding or storing a bowstring. The material reads rota; the final em begins emburulhão on the following line without a supplied hyphen.

runs.text: burulhão a corda do arco q̃ ſe leua de ſobreſe-

lines.note: Completes emburulhão, describing the string wound in the container. The string is carried as a spare for warfare; q̃ is the unexpanded abbreviation for que.
Completes sobreselente and the phrase 'to war'. The historical spelling of the spare item is preserved rather than modernized.
Tsurumi, tsurumu, tsurunda refers to animals mating. Ajunta- is confirmed by the visible u and continues as mento below; the abbreviated principal parts are kept literally.
Completes ajuntamento and specifies that animals are the subjects. The row belongs to the mating sense, not to the following cooking utensil.
Tsurunabe, alternatively tsurukake, is a type of iron pot. This confirms the cross-reference in c1-l044; pa- begins panela across the physical line break.

runs.text: nela de ferro, ou tacho que ſe toma com hum

lines.note: Completes panela and compares the object with an iron pan. It is lifted with an iron implement, whose attachment is described on the next row.
The iron implement catches in the pot's handles. Aſas has the long ſ visible in the scan and closes the description of tsurunabe.

Tsuru no ko is identified as the child of a great-grandchild, hence a great-great-grandchild. The Portuguese tataraneto and Japanese fimago no ko jointly support the damaged reading; the gloss is not the literal child of a crane here.

runs.text: Certo ferro como picão, ou ponta

lines.note: Tsuru no hashi names an iron tool resembling a pick or the point of a lever. The crane-bill image explains its form; the Portuguese technical comparison continues below.

runs.text: da lauanca com ſua hastea de pao pera arrancar

lines.note: Describes the wooden shaft and the tool's use in prying out stones. Arrancar is continuous at the right edge; the OCR's separated a rãcaro is not supported by the printed letters.
Completes the tool's purpose: removing stones or breaking them up. The scan gives desfazelas as one word; no extra space after des is retained.
Tsuru no motojiro identifies crane feathers used for arrows. Motojiro is a continuous printed compound, not the OCR's motoj ro; the abbreviated ſeruẽ continues the relative clause below.
The feathers are used to fletch arrows. Frechas is retained as the printed historical spelling rather than modern flechas.
Tsurusashi is a bowstring maker. This repeats the occupational sense associated with tsurukake in the first column and confirms the distinction from crane compounds.
Tsurutsuki is a small earthen vessel. The gloss reads vaſoſinho, with two long-ſ types, rather than the OCR's missing-syllable form; the comparison continues below.

runs.text: pucaro onde ſe metia o Cha moido.

lines.note: The container resembles a small cup and formerly held powdered tea. Cha is embedded in the Portuguese explanation; moido describes the tea as ground.
Tsurutsuruto is an adverb describing a manner of running or hurrying. The grammatical label Adu. belongs to the italic apparatus.
Completes the sense of hurrying one's pace. Tsurutsuruto hashiru exemplifies running in this manner; the Japanese reduplication has no internal space, unlike the OCR.

runs.text: Correr deſta maneira por breue eſpaço.

lines.note: The example is translated as running in this manner for a short distance or interval. This limits the preceding adverb's illustrated action.

runs.text: Hum certo officio entre os Bonzos

lines.note: Tsuusu is a particular monastic office. The scan supports long ſ and an unmarked final u, while bundled NINJAL confirms the lexical identity; the OCR's Teǔiù was not a usable Japanese form.

Identifies the monks as belonging to the Zen school. The enlarged label reads Ienxùs, with initial consonantal I and a grave over u; it is a Japanese-derived sect name within the Portuguese description.

runs.text: Certa era q̃ trepa pellas pare-

lines.note: Tsutakazura is a climbing ivy or vine. The scan has two z types in cazzura and the verb trepa, restoring letters lost by OCR; pare- continues as des below.
Completes paredes and gives trees as another support for the climbing plant. The definition does not require a more specific modern botanical identification.

runs.text: Ir como por atalhos, ou ao

lines.note: Tsutai, tsutoo, tsutoota means proceeding by a route or along successive supports. The gloss begins with going by shortcuts or alongside woods; the historical contracted principal parts retain their carons.

runs.text: longo do mato fora da estrada. ¶

lines.note: Completes the description of going along woodland off the road. Nami- begins the waves example below; the apparent extra ſ in OCR Namiſ- is the visible line-end division, not a Japanese consonant.

runs.text: Andar ſobre as ondas como gai-

lines.note: Nami-uo tsutoo means moving over the waves, compared with a gull. Gai- begins the divided Portuguese bird-name gaivota in the next row.
Completes gaiuota and introduces kozue wo tsutoo, moving along treetops. The scan shows a space before pol- and a division mark at the right edge.

runs.text: las pontas dos ramos como paßaro, ou bugio.

lines.note: Completes pollas pontas dos ramos: along the ends of branches like a bird or monkey. The comparison explains how the Japanese verb applies to moving between supports.

Sowa no kakeji wo tsutai yuku describes following a precarious mountain-side route. The printed caqegiuo is retained as historical romanization; the Portuguese begins the corresponding route description.

runs.text: algũas partes, ou caminhos ingremes ao longo

lines.note: Describes steep places or paths alongside a precipice. The form ingremes here is retained independently of the printed imgreme in c1-l035.
Finishes the precipice example, then introduces ishi wo tsutoo, proceeding by stones. The translation continues with repeated pedra below.

runs.text: pedra em pedra, ou como por ruim caminho,

lines.note: The movement is from stone to stone or along a bad path. The damaged first d still supplies pedra, correcting OCR peera; the line ends with a comma.

runs.text: ou depenedo empenedo por ſerra fragoſa.

lines.note: Adds moving from crag to crag through rugged mountains. The compact spacing depenedo empenedo is preserved, while the descender supports g in fragoſa rather than OCR ç.

runs.text: Caminho que ſe continua por par

lines.note: Tsutaimichi is a route continuing through difficult terrain. Par continues as tes on the next physical line; no terminal hyphen is supplied where none is securely printed.

runs.text: tes difficultoſas fora da estrada, ou por rode-

lines.note: Completes partes and describes difficult places away from the road or circuitous passages. Rode- continues as os below, retaining the printed physical division.
Completes rodeos and lists mountains and islands as the terrain traversed. The short row closes tsutaimichi before the Chinese timber entry.

runs.text: Hum pao, ou aruore da China boa pe-

lines.note: Tsuutan is a Chinese wood or tree suitable for workmanship. The damaged headword retains a visible caron over u, supported lexically by the bundled NINJAL entry; no modern species identification is imposed.
Completes pera fazer obra, suitability for making objects. This explains the practical value of the timber without specifying a particular craft.

runs.text: Couſa ſuja, ou vil: cõmummente ſe

lines.note: Tsutanai is glossed as low or vile, with a following qualification about use of persons. The historical evaluative sense is preserved instead of replacing it with the narrower modern 'unskilled'.
The gloss says the adjective is commonly applied to people. Kahou tsutanai mono describes a person with poor fortune; the medial t in tçutanai is supported by the headword and scan, not OCR r.
Translates the example as an unfortunate or unhappy person. This confirms that quafô concerns fortune in the preceding phrase.
Tsutanasa is the corresponding nominal form, lowliness or inadequacy. It is a short indented derivative without a new Portuguese gloss; the source's long ſ is retained.
Tsutanou is the adverbial form associated with tsutanai. The final character is o with a visible caron, not the OCR's ſi; its short indented row remains separate.

Tsutawari, tsutawaru, tsutawatta means being transmitted or descending through time. Deduzirſe is the historical Portuguese wording; the explanation continues on f493, while the lower conti- is a catchword rather than another body row.
Anticipates continuarſe at the beginning of f493. The complete visible catchword is retained as italic page furniture under its original stable ID.
